(Atlanta, Georgia) | college = [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] (2017–2018) | draft_year = 2018 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 7 | draft_team = [[Chicago Bulls]] | career_start = 2018 | years1 = {{nbay|2018|start}}–{{nbay|2020|end}} | team1 = [[Chicago Bulls]] | years2 = {{nbay|2020|end}}–present | team2 = [[Orlando Magic]] | highlights = * Second-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2018) * [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Freshman Team (2018) * [[Morgan Wootten National Player of the Year]] (2017) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2017]]) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport | Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|the {{USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-17 World Championship|FIBA U17 World Cup]]}} {{MedalGold| [[2016 FIBA Under-17 World Championship|2016 Spain]] | [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|National team]]}} }} '''Wendell Andre Carter Jr.''' ({{IPAc-en|w|ɛ|n|ˈ|d|ɛ|l}} {{respell|wen|DEL}};{{cite press release |author= |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=October 24, 2023 |access-date=May 18, 2024}} born April 16, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Orlando Magic]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. ==High school career== Carter attended [[Pace Academy]] in [[Atlanta, Georgia]].{{cite news|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/wendell-carter-college-decision-official-visits-duke-kentucky-harvard-082316|title=Meet the high school hoops star who could spurn Duke and Kentucky to attend Harvard|work=Fox Sports|date=August 23, 2016|access-date=March 7, 2017}} As a sophomore, he averaged 21.3 [[points per game]], 12.3 [[rebounds per game]], and 4.1 blocks while leading the Knights to a (27–3) record and a Georgia 6AA regional title. Carter would continue to develop his game during the summer of 2015 where he led his AAU team, Georgia Stars, to a [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] (EYBL) Peach Jam championship and was named Co-MVP alongside [[Jared Harper]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.d1circuit.com/news_article/show/536223|title=Wendell Carter, Jared Harper share MVP honor for powerhouse Peach Jam Champs|last=Kinsky|first=Alec|date=July 21, 2015|publisher=D1 Circuit|access-date=February 12, 2020}} after his sophomore season, Carter also earned the Georgia Region 6 AA Player of the Year and second-team Atlanta Tipoff Club All Metro-honors. In his junior season in 2015–16, he averaged 21.6 [[points per game]] and 13.6 [[rebounds per game]]. In the state finals game, Carter scored 30 points and recorded 20 rebounds to lead Pace Academy to win the 2016 Georgia class AA state Championship.{{Cite web|url=https://www.ajc.com/blog/high-school-sports/class-boys-pace-academy-manchester/kw3xF7JHz7QX2CI9HPkFkN/|title=Class AA boys: Pace Academy 65, Manchester 43|last=Awtrey|first=Stan|date=March 4, 2016|publisher=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution|access-date=February 12, 2020}} He was named an honorable mention All-American by the Naismith Trophy, a first-team Junior All-American by MaxPreps, the Georgia Class AA Player of the year, the Atlanta/South Fulton Player of the Year, and a first-team all-state selection as a junior.{{Cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211644090|title=Wendell Carter – 2017–18 – Men's Basketball|access-date=December 12, 2017|archive-date=December 12, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171212084919/http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211644090|url-status=dead}} In the spring and summer of 2016, Carter competed for the AAU team, Team CP3 sponsored by [[San Antonio Spurs]] point guard [[Chris Paul]]. He averaged 16.8 points per game and 10.2 rebounds per game on the Nike EYBL Circuit, earning second-team All-EYBL honoree.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/ncbrecruiting/on-the-trail/insider/post/_/id/15852|title=Top-5 prospect Wendell Carter isn't all about basketball, and he doesn't care|last=Borzello|first=Jeff|date=June 28, 2016|website=ESPN.com|access-date=July 6, 2017}} [[File:20170329 MCDAAG Wendell Carter Jr. 1-handed dunk (5).jpg|thumb|Carter finishing a dunk at the [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2017 McDonald's All-American Game]] ]] As a senior, he averaged 22.7 [[Point (basketball)|points]], 15.5 [[rebounds]], and 5.8 blocks while leading the Knights to a Georgia class 3A state championship on March 9, 2017.{{Cite web|url=https://hoopseen.com/news/general/201703/pace-holds-court-against-liberty-county|title=Pace holds the court against Liberty County|last=Young|first=Justin|date=March 4, 2017|publisher=Hoopseen|access-date=February 12, 2020}} Carter was named Georgia All-Classification Player of the Year, Gatorade Georgia Player of the Year, first-team All-America honors from the Naismith Trophy, second-team accolades from USA Today, and third-team recognition from MaxPreps. Carter played in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]], [[Nike Hoop Summit]], and the [[McDonald's All-American Game]], where he finished with 10 points, 5 rebounds, and 3 assists.{{cite web|url=https://www.usatodayhss.com/2017/duke-signee-wendell-carter-jr-honored-for-jordan-brand-classic|title=Duke signee Wendell Carter Jr honored for Jordan Brand Classic|date=February 2, 2017|website=USA Today High School Sports|access-date=August 31, 2024}} Off of the court, Carter was named the [[Morgan Wootten National Player of the Year]],{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/18842896/wendell-carter-duke-blue-devils-recruit-wins-morgan-wootten-national-player-year-award|title=Wendell Carter wins Morgan Wootten National POY award|first=Paul|last=Biancardi|work=ESPN|date=March 7, 2017|access-date=March 7, 2017}}{{cite news|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2017/03/07/wendell-carter-morgan-wootten-poy|title=Duke signee Wendell Carter Jr. named Morgan Wootten Player of the Year|publisher=Sports Illustrated|date=March 7, 2017|access-date=March 7, 2017}} which goes to student-athletes who exemplify outstanding character, leadership, and academics. He earned a 3.8 GPA in high school and won his school's Lance and Shield Award as a top scholar-athlete.{{Cite news|url=https://andscape.com/features/wendell-carter-jr-duke|title=Duke signee Wendell Carter Jr. and his parents have basketball in the blood and academics on their minds|last=Spears|first=Marc J.|date=April 14, 2017|work=[[Andscape]]|access-date=June 22, 2018|language=en-US}} Carter in 2018]] Before the start of his freshman season, Carter was projected to start at power forward for the [[2017-18 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2017-18 Blue Devils]] forming a frontcourt tandem with [[Marvin Bagley III]].{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/2017/07/25/wendell-carter-duke-blue-devils-recruiting|title=Wendell Carter Fills and Immediate Need for Duke at Power Robertson Trophy|Robertson]], and [[Karl Malone Award|Malone]] preseason watch lists.{{cite web|url=https://goduke.com/news/2017/10/19/211673761.aspx|title=Two Duke Freshmen Named to Karl Malone Watch List|date=October 19, 2017|publisher=[[Duke Blue Devils]]|access-date=February 27, 2024}} On November 18, Carter scored 20 points and 11 rebounds in a 78–61 victory over [[Southern Jaguars basketball|Southern]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2017/11/17/carter-jr-scores-20-no-1-duke-beats-southern-78-61/107796520/|title=Wendell Carter Jr scores 20 to Pace top-ranked Duke past southern|work=USA Today|date=November 18, 2017|access-date=February 12, 2020}} On November 20, Carter was named ACC rookie of the week.{{Cite Conference]]|access-date=November 20, 2017}} Against the [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana Hoosiers]], he had a double-double with 18 points and 12 rebounds despite being in foul trouble to lift Duke in a 91–81 win.{{Cite web|url=http://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/college/article188900019.html|title=Duke's Wendell Carter Jr. hoping to stay out of foul trouble as Blue Devils enter conference play|last=Alexander|first=Jonathan|date=December 8, 2017|website=The Charlotte Observer}} On December 20, 2017, Carter scored a career-high 27 points in a 104–40 blowout win against [[Evansville Purple Aces men's basketball|Evansville]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/400986156|title=Carter leads No.4 Duke to 104-40 rout of Evansville|date=December 20, 2017|website=[[ESPN.com]]|access-date=September 7, 2024}} On December 26, 2017, Carter earned his second ACC rookie of the week honor.{{Cite 60-44|date=February 24, 2018|website=[[ESPN.com]]|access-date=February 27, 2024}} On the season, Carter averaged 13.1 points and 9.1 rebounds per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2018/03/carter-2018-player-review-model|title=Duke men's basketball 2017–18 player review: Wendell Carter Jr|last=Model|first=Michael|date=March 29, 2018|publisher=[[Duke Chronicle]]|access-date=March 30, 2018}} Carter had one of the best freshman seasons for a power forward/center in Duke history where he would finish second all-time for Duke freshman with (335) rebounds, (76) blocked shots and (16) career double-doubles. Following Duke's loss in the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA men's basketball tournament]], Carter announced his intention to forgo his final three seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2018 NBA draft]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23201541/duke-blue-devils-wendell-carter-jr-declaring-nba-draft|title=Duke's Wendell Carter Jr. declaring for NBA draft|date=April 16, 2018|work=[[ESPN]]}} Carter was subsequently named both Second team All-ACC and ACC All-Freshman teams.{{Cite web|url=http://www.theacc.com/news/2018/3/4/mens-basketball-acc-announces-all-conference-team-postseason-awards.aspx?path=mbball|title=ACC Announces All-Conference Team, Postseason Awards|website=TheACC.com|publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|date=March 4, 2018|access-date=February 13, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Chicago Bulls (2018–2021)=== On June 21, 2018, Carter was selected with the seventh overall pick by the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/basketball/bulls/ct-spt-bulls-wendell-carter-draft-20180621-story.html|title=Bulls take Duke big man Wendell Carter Jr. with 7th pick in NBA draft|last=Johnson|first=K.C.|work=Chicago Tribune|access-date=June 22, 2018|language=en-US}} On July 3, 2018, Carter officially signed with the Bulls.{{cite web |title=Bulls sign Carter Jr. and Hutchison |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-carter-jr-and-hutchison |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 4, 2018 |language=en}} On October 18, he made his NBA debut, scoring eight points and recording three rebounds, three assists and a block against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]],{{Cite news|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/bulls/wendell-carter-jr-gets-early-learning-experience-against-embiid-sixers|title=Wendell Carter Jr. gets early lesson against Embiid, Sixers|last=Hudrick|first=Paul|date=October 19, 2018|work=NBC Sports Chicago}} Four days later, Carter recorded career-highs in rebounds (9) and assists (4) against the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070725|title=Jordan gets another double-double as Mavs top Bulls 115–109|date=October 22, 2018|website=ESPN.com}} On October 31, 2018, Carter scored a season high 25 points with eight rebounds, five assists, three blocks and three steals in a 107–108 overtime loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070787|title=Millsap's putback gives Nuggets 108–107 win over Bulls in OT|date=October 31, 2018|work=ESPN.com|access-date=November 1, 2018}} He would break that amount on November 30 with 28 points scored in a loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]]. On March 24, 2019, Carter was ruled out for the remainder of the season with left thumb surgery.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2019/03/23/chicago-bulls-shut-down-carter-jr-hutchison-rest-season|title=Bulls shut down rookies Carter Jr., Hutchison |date=March 24, 2019 |website=NBA.com |access-date=April 12, 2019}} ===Orlando Magic (2021–present)=== On March 25, 2021, Carter and [[Otto Porter]] were traded to the [[Orlando Magic]] in exchange for [[Nikola Vučević]] and [[Al-Farouq Aminu]]. Orlando also received two future first-round draft picks.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-acquire-wendell-carter-jr-otto-porter-jr-chicago-bulls-nikola-vucevic-al-farouq-aminu-trade-20210325|title=Magic Acquire Wendell Carter Jr., Otto Porter Jr. and Two First Round Draft Picks From Chicago|date=March 25, 2021|work=NBA.com}} On October 16, 2021, Carter signed a four-year, $50 million rookie scale extension with the Magic.{{Cite |date=October 16, 2021 |access-date=February 23, 2022}} On March 20, 2022, Carter scored a career-high 30 points in a 90–85 win against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web |last1=Scanlon |first1=Dick |title=Carter, Magic hand Thunder 9th straight loss, 90-85 |url=https://apnews.com/article/orlando-magic-oklahoma-city-thunder-nba-sports-oklahoma-city-a2b9eb84879860f5255351e08215e213 |website=Associated Press |access-date=November 27, 2022 |date=March 20, 2022}} Carter matched his career-high of 30 points in a 116–108 loss on November 1, 2022, against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web |title=Gilgeous-Alexander's 34 help Thunder push win streak to 4 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468260 |website=ESPN |access-date=November 28, 2022 |date=November 1, 2022}} On December 11, Carter scored a double-double of 20 points and 10 rebounds in a 114–97 win against the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468332|title=Carter, Ross lead Magic to 114-97 win over Suns|date=December 11, 2022|website=[[ESPN.com]]|access-date=September 4, 2024}} On December 18, Carter scored 21 points and 8 rebounds in a 108–107 victory over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468382|title=Suggs nails 3, Magic beat Bulls 108-107 after blowing lead|date=November 19, 2022|website=[[ESPN.com]]|access-date=September 4, 2024}} On December 29, he was suspended by the NBA for one game without pay due to coming off the bench during an altercation in a game against the [[Detroit Pistons]] the day before.{{cite web |title=NBA announces suspensions from Pistons-Magic game |url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-announces-pistons-magic-suspensions |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 31, 2022 |date=December 29, 2022}} On October 7, 2024, Carter and the Magic agreed to a three–year, $58.7 million contract extension.{{Cite web |date=October 8, 2024 |title=Magic extend center Carter on 3-year, $59M deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/41671730/magic-wendell-carter-jr-agree-3-year-59m-extension |access-date=2025-12-11 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} ==National team career== Carter played with the United States U17 team at the [[FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup]], where he won gold. As well, he was named to the [[FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup All-Tournament Team|All-Tournament Team]], along with teammate [[Collin Sexton]].{{cite web
